evidence_summary: In mouse cochlear development, Sema5B-Fc reduced type I spiral-ganglion terminal branch number and increased branch length; Sema5B loss caused the opposite phenotype, while conditional Plxna1 loss increased branching, supporting a Sema5B/PlexinA1 receptor-dependent branch-refinement output.
limitations: The study identifies PlexinA1 as a responding receptor in a context where SGNs also express PlexinA3; Sema5B-Fc activates Plexin-As and does not provide a purified pair-specific binding measurement. Developmental auditory model only. High is limited to the cited non-direct relay/function record; no binary binding, TF, or SCI-transfer inference is made.

evidence_summary: In adult mouse dentate gyrus, Sema7A inhibited early neural-progenitor proliferation through PlexinC1 in vitro and in vivo; Sema7A and PlexinC1 knockout mice showed concordant increased proliferation, while later dendritic effects used beta1-integrin receptors rather than PlexinC1.
limitations: This is a stage-specific adult hippocampal model. PlexinC1 and beta1-integrin effects are receptor-context dependent; the paper does not define a complete intracellular kinase-to-TF cascade or SCI receiver-cell mechanism. High is limited to the cited non-direct relay/function record; no binary binding, TF, or SCI-transfer inference is made.

evidence_summary: In primary mouse hepatocytes, 30 microM holo-transferrin induced rapid, transient ERK1/2 phosphorylation; serum plus holo-transferrin enhanced and prolonged the response, and 10 microM U0-126 blunted the holo-transferrin-dependent hepcidin response.
limitations: The primary full text supports ligand-triggered TFR2-associated signaling in primary hepatocytes, not purified TFR2 binding affinity or a universal TFR2 kinase pathway. The article notes that TFR2 attribution is favored by transferrin subtype/context comparisons; TFR2 remains an iron-sensing/complex node. High is limited to the cited non-direct relay/function record; no binary binding, TF, or SCI-transfer inference is made.
